symbols.def: The attainable treated-neighbor fractions for vertex \(a\); weights have no off-support coordinates.

symbols.name: mH

symbols.name: ZH

symbols.name: AH

standard.name: Minimum-degree-two condition for quadratic exposure reproduction
Independent Bernoulli assignment with propensity one half
No-interference null within the network linear-in-means class
Gao et al. squared spillover separation expressed on the RMS scale

definitions.name: Repeated-motif graph
definitions.construction: \(G_r=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^rH\) on \(\mathcal I_r=\{(k,a):1\le k\le r,\ a\in V_H\}\), with edges only within copies.

definitions.name: Unbiased quadratic weight class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal W_H=\{w\in\prod_{a\in V_H}\mathbb R^{\mathcal E_a(H)}:\mathbb E_{Z_H}[w_a\{T_a(Z_H)\}]=0,\ \mathbb E_{Z_H}[T_a(Z_H)w_a\{T_a(Z_H)\}]=0,\ \mathbb E_{Z_H}[T_a(Z_H)^2w_a\{T_a(Z_H)\}]=1\text{ for every }a\in V_H\}\).

definitions.name: Motif assignment table
definitions.construction: Enumerate \(\mathcal A_H=\{0,1\}^{V_H}\) in lexicographic order. Each of its \(2^h\) rows records \(z_a\), \(t_a(z)=d_H(a)^{-1}\sum_{c\in N_H(a)}z_c\), and \(y_{b,a}(z)=b_{a,1}+b_{a,2}z_a+b_{a,3}t_a(z)\) for every \(a\in V_H\).

definitions.name: Exact robust semialgebraic variance program
definitions.construction: From the \(2^h\)-row table \(\mathcal A_H\), form \(F_H(w,b)=2^{-h}\sum_z[S_H(w,b;z)-2^{-h}\sum_{z'}S_H(w,b;z')]^2\). The program \(\mathfrak P_H\) minimizes \(q\) over \(m_H=\sum_a\{d_H(a)+1\}\le h^2\) support-indexed weight coordinates and \(q\), subject to the \(3h\) exposure-moment equalities and the robust constraint \(q\ge F_H(w,b)\) for every \(b\in\mathbb R^{3h}\) satisfying \(-1\le b_{a,1}+b_{a,2}z_a+b_{a,3}t_a(z)\le1\) for all \(a\) and all \(2^h\) rows \(z\). It has \(3h\) nuisance variables, \(2h2^h\) displayed linear schedule inequalities, and a variance polynomial of degree two in \(w\) and four in \(b\); quantifier elimination gives an exact finite certificate, while row enumeration gives a direct numerical program.

definitions.name: Two-motif exact certificate
definitions.construction: For \(H=K_3\) and \(H=C_4\), build \(\mathfrak P_H\) from the lexicographic \(2^h\)-row assignment table. Since every vertex has degree two, row reduction of the three exposure moments gives \(w_a(0)=8\), \(w_a(1/2)=-8\), and \(w_a(1)=8\). Eliminate the \(3h\) bounded-schedule variables from \(q\ge F_H(w,b)\) using rational univariate representation. The \(K_3\) instance has eight assignment rows, nine weight coordinates, nine nuisance variables, and forty-eight assignment-indexed signed schedule inequalities; after removing duplicates, write \(p_i=y_i(0,0)\), \(q_i=y_i(1,0)\), \(r_i=y_i(0,1)\), and \(s_i=q_i+r_i-p_i=y_i(1,1)\), so its legal domain is the twelve polynomial inequalities \(1-p_i^2\ge0\), \(1-q_i^2\ge0\), \(1-r_i^2\ge0\), and \(1-s_i^2\ge0\) for \(i=1,2,3\). The exact upper certificate is the quantified implication that these twelve inequalities imply \(F_{K_3}(w,b)\le v_{K_3}\). The \(C_4\) instance has sixteen rows, twelve weight coordinates, twelve nuisance variables, and one hundred twenty-eight assignment-indexed signed schedule inequalities. For \(K_3\), let \(x_\triangle=(-13+2\sqrt{55})/17\), the unique root in \((0,1)\) of \(17x^2+26x-3=0\), and take the three vertex coefficient rows to be \((1,-(1+x_\triangle),-(1-x_\triangle))\), \((1,0,0)\), and \((-1,2,0)\). For assignments \(000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111\), the corresponding outcome rows are \((1,1,-1)\), \(((1+x_\triangle)/2,1,1)\), \(((1+x_\triangle)/2,1,-1)\), \((x_\triangle,1,1)\), \((-x_\triangle,1,-1)\), \((-(1+x_\triangle)/2,1,1)\), \((-(1+x_\triangle)/2,1,-1)\), and \((-1,1,1)\); hence every displayed outcome lies in \([-1,1]\). The resulting statistic rows are \(24\), four copies of \(-2x_\triangle^2-4x_\triangle-2\), two copies of \(8x_\triangle^2-16\), and \(24\), with mean \((1-x_\triangle)^2\) and variance \(17x_\triangle^4+12x_\triangle^3-58x_\triangle^2+12x_\triangle+209\). Quantifier elimination of the displayed implication certifies the matching upper bound; equivalently, \(v_{K_3}\) is the unique root in \((209,210)\) of \(4913v^2-1537792v+106463232=0\), and equality holds at this legal schedule. For \(C_4\), the legal constant schedule \(y_{b,a}(z)=1\) has statistic rows \(32,0,0,-32,0,32,-32,0,0,-32,32,0,-32,0,0,32\), and elimination certifies the matching upper bound \(v_{C_4}=512\). Independently sum \(T_a(z)^4\) over the same rows to compute \(\xi_H\).

definitions.name: Exact worst-null calibration
definitions.construction: Fix \(w\) and enumerate all \(2^{rh}\) assignments \(z\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal I_r}\). Under the null, parameterize each unit by the two values \(x_{ka,0}=\beta_{ka,1}\) and \(x_{ka,1}=\beta_{ka,1}+\beta_{ka,2}\) in \([-1,1]\), and tabulate the resulting quadratic polynomial \(Q_{r,w}(z;x)\). Introduce threshold \(t\) and boundary-randomization \(u\), enumerate the finitely many strict, equal, and lower sign patterns of \(Q_{r,w}(z;x)-t\), and apply exact quantifier elimination over \(x\in[-1,1]^{2n}\), \(t\), and \(u\) to enforce the worst-null tail-mass inequality. Minimizing \(t\) yields \(c_{\alpha,r}(w)\), and maximizing the feasible \(u\) at that threshold yields \(\gamma_{\alpha,r}(w)\) in \(\phi_{\alpha,r,w}\).

definitions.name: Motif affinity factor
definitions.construction: Compute \(\xi_H=2^{-h}\sum_{z\in\mathcal A_H}\sum_{a\in V_H}T_a(z)^4\) from the assignment table and set \(C_{\cos}=64\pi^4/5\). The graph calculation uses exactly \(h\,2^h\) exposure-power evaluations.

definitions.name: Assignment-preserving hard subexperiment
definitions.construction: Draw \(Z\) independently of coefficients. Under \(P_{0,a}\), draw \(\beta_{ka,1}\) independently with density \(h_0\) and set \(\beta_{ka,2}=\beta_{ka,3}=0\). Under \(P_{1,a}\), use the same baseline law, set \(\beta_{ka,2}=0\), and draw \(\beta_{ka,3}=aS_{ka}\) with independent Rademacher signs \(S_{ka}\). Observe \((Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\); every alternative draw has \(g_r(\beta)=a^2\), hence belongs to \(\mathcal B_{1,r}(H,a^2)\).

definitions.name: Orbit-likelihood handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathfrak O_H\) by quotienting the one-motif assignment--observation experiment under \(\operatorname{Aut}(H)\), retaining assignment labels and null and alternative schedule-orbit likelihood kernels, then tensorize across \(r\) copies.

statements.statement: Theorem 1. The functional \(w\mapsto\sup_{b\in\mathcal B_H}\operatorname{Var}_{Z_H}S_H(w,b;Z_H)\) is coercive on \(\mathcal W_H\): for the Euclidean norm on the \(m_H\) attainable-support coordinates, its value diverges whenever \(\|w\|_2\to\infty\) with \(w\in\mathcal W_H\). Primal and dual optimizers exist and \[v_H=\min_{w\in\mathcal W_H}\max_{b\in\mathcal B_H}\operatorname{Var}_{Z_H}S_H(w,b;Z_H)=\max_{\Pi\in\mathcal P(\mathcal B_H)}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_H}\int_{\mathcal B_H}\operatorname{Var}_{Z_H}S_H(w,b;Z_H)\,d\Pi(b)=D_H.\] Moreover, \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=v_H/(rh^2)\), and \(\mathfrak P_H\) has optimal value \(v_H\). A feasible \(w^*\) minimizes if and only if an attained \(\Pi^*\), supported on its variance contact set, makes the integrated variance gradient orthogonal to the tangent space of \(\mathcal W_H\).
statements.justification: Attainment and contacts make the scale graph-computable and characterize every optimal weight.
statements.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026, arXiv version 2, Section 4 and Appendix B fix one feasible Bernoulli quadratic weight, while Proposition 4.1 gives an MSE envelope from the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4. None gives the attained repeated-motif conditional-variance constant, its robust program, or its integral-of-conditional-variance dual.
statements.consumer: In the LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network experiments of PougetAbadieEtAl2019, the known repeated local graph motif determines which feasible exposure-quadratic weight minimizes the worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant; that motif-level choice sets the exact test threshold and power calibration relative to deploying the fixed GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 weight.

statements.statement: Lemma 2. For every \(|s|\le1/2\), \[H^2(h_0,g_s)\le C_{\cos}s^4,\qquad C_{\cos}=64\pi^4/5.\] The priors in \(\mathrm{def:hard\text{-}subexperiment}\) are supported on \(\mathcal B_{0,r}(H)\) and \(\mathcal B_{1,r}(H,a^2)\), the marginal law of \(Z\) agrees, and \[H^2(P_{0,a},P_{1,a})\le C_{\cos}r\xi_Ha^4.\]
statements.justification: Symmetric shifts cancel first-order information, and the eighth-order boundary controls support change.
statements.gap: The design-based Le Cam and classical quadratic-prior papers do not prove this uniform assignment-conditional inequality.
statements.consumer: The explicit constant evaluates every test and can be compared directly with the optimized motif variance.

statements.statement: Theorem 3. For any minimizer \(w^*\), the assignment and sign-pattern enumeration in \(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}calibration}\) terminates after finitely many semialgebraic feasibility decisions, computes \(c_{\alpha,r}(w^*)\) and \(\gamma_{\alpha,r}(w^*)\), and gives \(\phi_{\alpha,r,w^*}\) worst-null rejection probability at most \(\alpha\) for every \(r\). Also \(c_{\alpha,r}(w^*)\le\sqrt{V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r/\alpha}\), and its worst-alternative power is at least \(1-\eta\) whenever \[\delta_{\mathrm{sq}}\ge\sqrt{V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r/\alpha}+\sqrt{V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r/\eta}.\]
statements.justification: With the Bernoulli-half reproduction identity imported from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B, finite-sample calibration closes the nonsharp-null gap without losing the fourth-root scale.
statements.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026, arXiv version 2, Proposition 4.1 supplies an MSE envelope using Lemmas S3--S4; it does not compute an exact worst-null critical value over bounded schedules. TiwariBasu2026 proves asymptotic validity for a different statistic.
statements.consumer: LinkedIn can audit the full feed-ranking arm and attach a guaranteed detectable spillover magnitude.

statements.statement: Theorem 4. For fixed \(H\), every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1-\alpha)\), every \(r\), every \(\phi\in\Psi_{\alpha,r}\), and every \(\delta_{\mathrm{sq}}\ge0\) satisfying \(\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{sq}}}\le\sqrt{\varepsilon}L_H(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}\), \[\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal B_{1,r}(H,\delta_{\mathrm{sq}})}\mathbb E_{Z,U}(\phi\mid\beta)\le\alpha+\varepsilon.\] Here \(L_H=\{h^2/(C_{\cos}\xi_Hv_H)\}^{1/4}\) is computed from the same \(2^h\)-row assignment table and optimized motif variance program as the upper statistic.
statements.justification: An all-test converse makes the scale an information bound rather than a quadratic limitation.
statements.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026, arXiv version 2, Proposition 4.1 is an MSE upper envelope supported by Lemmas S3--S4 and has no all-test converse; Tiwari--Basu study power by simulation, and Kandiros et al. target estimation.
statements.consumer: The theorem identifies when no analysis of the same Bernoulli arm can reliably detect smaller spillovers.

statements.statement: Theorem 5. For fixed \(H\), \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1-\alpha)\), \[\sqrt{1-\alpha-\eta}\,L_H(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}\le r^*_{\alpha,\eta}(H,r)\le\{\alpha^{-1/2}+\eta^{-1/2}\}^{1/2}(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}.\] Thus \(r^*_{\alpha,\eta}(H,r)\asymp r^{-1/4}\). The identity \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=v_H/(rh^2)\), its attainment, the computable lower constant \(L_H\), exact worst-null calibration, and the all-test converse form a graph-specific repeated-motif testing frontier. As a sanity reduction, when every vertex has degree two, the three attainable-support moment equations force \(\mathcal W_H=\{w^G\}\), so the optimized quadratic statistic coincides with the fixed Section 4 and Appendix B weight of GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026; there is no motifwise variance improvement over that fixed weight in this degree-two case.
statements.justification: The theorem makes optimized conditional variance both sufficient and necessary.
statements.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B construct the quadratic statistic, Proposition 4.1 gives its \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope, and Lemmas S3--S4 supply the variance ingredients; they do not identify the attained repeated-motif conditional-variance constant, exact composite-null calibration, or its necessity for testing. Tiwari--Basu leave theoretical power open.
statements.consumer: A platform can report a graph-specific detection floor before running the experiment.

statements.statement: Proposition 6. For each of the nonisomorphic minimum-degree-two motifs \(K_3\) and \(C_4\), the support-indexed class \(\mathcal W_H\) is the singleton \(w^G\), with \(w_a(0)=8\), \(w_a(1/2)=-8\), and \(w_a(1)=8\). The legal eight-row \(K_3\) schedule and elimination certificate in \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}motif\text{-}certificate}\) give \[v_{K_3}=\frac{768896+35200\sqrt{55}}{4913}=209.6369197529\ldots,\qquad v_{C_4}=512.\] Assignment enumeration gives \(\xi_{K_3}=27/32\) and \(\xi_{C_4}=9/8\), hence \[L_{K_3}=\left\{\frac{5}{6\pi^4v_{K_3}}\right\}^{1/4}=0.0799259622\ldots,\qquad L_{C_4}=\left\{\frac{5}{2304\pi^4}\right\}^{1/4}=0.0687024160\ldots.\] Consequently \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=v_{K_3}/(9r)=23.2929910837\ldots/r\) for triangles and \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=32/r\) for four-cycles. The all-test lower constants in Theorem 4 are respectively \(0.0799259622\ldots\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) and \(0.0687024160\ldots\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) times \((V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}\).
statements.justification: Two exact nonisomorphic motif calculations make both sides of the frontier operational and expose geometry-dependent constants beyond degree alone.
statements.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 gives a degree-based MSE envelope for the same fixed weight but does not evaluate these worst-schedule repeated-motif constants or pair them with explicit all-test Hellinger constants.
statements.consumer: Triangle and four-cycle clusters give separate exact benchmarks for implementation and pre-experiment power audits.

statements.statement: Open-ended Question 7. Determine the limiting minimax power function when \(r^{1/4}\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{sq}}}\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\), and decide whether an exactly calibrated quadratic minimizer attains it among \(\Psi_{\alpha,r}\). If not, characterize the strict gain of a nonquadratic invariant test.
statements.justification: Rate optimality does not decide whether quadratic compression loses a motif-specific power constant.
statements.gap: No cited source derives the finite invariant composite testing experiment needed for exact procedural optimality.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether a platform should deploy a more complex motif-likelihood test.

sampling_model.design: Known independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/2\); assignment is the only sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population on \(r\) disjoint copies of a fixed known motif \(H\) with minimum degree two.
sampling_model.treatment: Each \(Z_{ka}\) is independent, and exposure is \(T_{ka}(Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every motif assignment has positive probability \(2^{-h}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Baselines and direct effects are fixed adversarial nuisances; converse priors mix deterministic schedules only as a proof device.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: ArXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B construct the Bernoulli quadratic-weight statistic; Proposition 4.1 states its \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope using the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4.
Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic validity for an estimated-residual randomization test while leaving theoretical power open.
Section 5 gives the Riesz representer and unbiased estimator and notes possible gains from alternative weights.
Proposition 3 gives a design-based Le Cam lower bound for squared-error estimation.
Theorems 1 and 2 match quadratic tests and mixture lower bounds in random-design regression.
Proposition 1 and Section 5 obtain exact nonsharp-null tests through focal artificial experiments.
Theorems 1 and 2 give valid conditional tests when the focal statistic is imputable.
The paper gives conditional tests for hierarchical interference specifications.

tldr: Using the Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities and quadratic weight imported from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B, this project studies a fixed network motif repeated under Bernoulli assignment. A \(2^h\)-row assignment table yields an exact robust semialgebraic program for the attained worst-schedule assignment-conditional variance and its least-favourable-prior dual. For a LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network experiment with a known repeated local motif, the contact-set certificate selects among feasible exposure-quadratic weights by the smallest worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant, thereby fixing the test threshold and power calibration relative to the published Gao et al. weight. The same table gives the explicit affinity factor \(L_H\), with certified comparisons for the nonisomorphic motifs \(K_3\) and \(C_4\). The optimal quadratic statistic is calibrated at finite-sample level over every bounded no-spillover schedule, and its fourth-root RMS signal scale is unavoidable for every measurable test. On degree-two motifs the feasible weight equals Gao et al.'s published weight, so the new content is the attained motif constant, exact calibration, and matching testing necessity rather than a strict improvement of the weight. Whether the quadratic test also attains the exact local power constant remains open.

project_justification.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B supply the Bernoulli quadratic-weight construction, while Proposition 4.1 gives a \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope from Lemmas S3--S4; available randomization tests provide validity without a theoretical local-power frontier.
project_justification.niche: Repeated fixed motifs isolate graph geometry from growing-degree asymptotics while preserving the practical Bernoulli design.
project_justification.fill: The project computes the attained variance saddle from a \(2^h\)-row robust semialgebraic program, uses its contact set to select the feasible exposure-quadratic weight with the smallest worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant for a known repeated motif, derives exact worst-null calibration by finite assignment and sign-pattern enumeration, and proves a matching all-test fourth-root lower bound with an explicit motif-computable Hellinger constant and certified \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) comparisons.

related_work: The Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities and quadratic weight are imported as background from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B. Its Proposition 4.1 gives a \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope using the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4. This paper is an informed-by comparator: on degree-two motifs the feasible weight is exactly Gao et al.'s weight, while the new repeated-motif results identify its attained worst-schedule conditional-variance constant, provide exact composite-null calibration, and prove the same fourth-root scale necessary for all tests. TiwariBasu2026 establishes validity for a different residual test and motivates the open power question. HarshawSavjeWang2022 informs the finite-dimensional Riesz geometry. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 informs the design-based Le Cam reduction. CommingesDalalyan2013 informs fourth-root quadratic testing. AtheyEcklesImbens2018, BasseFellerToulis2019, and HoshinoYanagi2026 provide focal-conditioning benchmarks without being theorem-level targets. Ni2026 surveys the design--power tension. PougetAbadieEtAl2019 supplies the LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network deployment: given the known repeated local motif, Theorem 1 selects among feasible exposure-quadratic weights by worst bounded-schedule conditional variance, which determines the exact test threshold and power calibration relative to the fixed GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 weight.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicit hard-prior calculation proves a constant-factor converse. The bound \(H^2(P_{0,a},P_{1,a})\le C_{\cos}r\xi_Ha^4\) does not identify the exact local likelihood experiment or establish quadratic sufficiency. The exact local power function and quadratic completeness remain in Open-ended Question 7.
honest_scope: The claims to prove are coercivity of the worst-schedule variance functional, variance-game attainment and duality, exact finite-sample control through explicit enumeration, the explicit fourth-order affinity lemma, a constant-factor all-test frontier, and exact motif certificates. The Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities, Gao et al.'s squared-separation convention, and their quadratic weight are imported background from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B and are not solve targets. On degree-two motifs the feasible weight equals the published weight, so no strict weight improvement is claimed. The exact local power curve and any nonquadratic advantage remain open. Exact elimination of the eight- and sixteen-row programs supplies the stated \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) values; the decimals report algebraic certificates rather than simulation output.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The arXiv version 2 source was opened. Section 4, Proposition 4.1, Appendix B, and Lemmas S3--S4 were read. Section 4 and Appendix B contain the Bernoulli quadratic-weight construction; Proposition 4.1 states the MSE envelope, and Lemmas S3--S4 provide its variance ingredients rather than an attained repeated-motif analysis.
seed_details.kernel: For Bernoulli assignment on disjoint copies of a fixed motif, prove \(r^*_{\alpha,\eta}\asymp(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}\), where \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r\) is the attained worst-schedule conditional variance computed by an explicit \(2^h\)-row semialgebraic program, with an exact finite-sample upper test, an explicit motif-computable lower constant, and a converse over all measurable tests.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Gao et al.'s covariance envelope by the exact motifwise conditional-variance game; for the converse, replace consistency arguments by a symmetric translated-density mixture whose first-order score cancels conditional on assignment.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches combining interference specification testing, repeated motifs, quadratic minimax power, and fourth-root separation found the cited upper tests and classical quadratic-functional theory but no design-based local minimax theorem for this target.
seed_details.red_team: A referee could call the fourth-root rate immediate because Gao et al. estimate a squared signal.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their result supplies neither an attained repeated-motif variance constant, exact composite-null calibration, nor a lower bound against nonquadratic tests; on degree-two motifs the feasible weight itself is unchanged.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim includes an explicit statistic, a graph-specific variance object, exact level control, and an all-test converse uniform over a compact schedule class.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The arXiv source was opened. The Introduction, the positivity and Riesz-representer results in Section 5, the estimator construction, and the Conclusion were read. seed_details.kernel: Characterize every minimizer of worst-schedule conditional variance among exposure-moment reproducing quadratic weights by an attained Sion dual and a contact-set stationarity certificate.

novelty_justification: The two closest results are GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 and TiwariBasu2026. In arXiv version 2, Gao et al. Section 4 and Appendix B construct the identical support-indexed quadratic statistic, Proposition 4.1 gives its \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope, and Lemmas S3--S4 supply the variance ingredients. Gao et al. are treated as informed-by background: on degree-two motifs the feasible weight is exactly their fixed weight, and no strict motifwise variance improvement is claimed. Their paper does not identify the attained repeated-motif conditional-variance constant, calibrate the composite null exactly, or prove a testing converse. Tiwari and Basu prove validity for a different residual test and explicitly leave theoretical power open. The contribution is an operational \(2^h\)-row semialgebraic variance saddle whose contact set selects the feasible exposure-quadratic weight minimizing worst bounded-schedule conditional variance for a known motif, exact full-sample calibration, an explicit fourth-order assignment-preserving affinity constant, and certified \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) calculations that rule out every measurable test below the same attained scale. In the PougetAbadieEtAl2019 LinkedIn-style deployment, this selection determines the test threshold and power calibration relative to the fixed GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 weight. CommingesDalalyan2013 has the classical geometry but not fixed schedules; KandirosHarshawSavje2026 has the design-based Le Cam discipline but not local quadratic testing.
